text: Which is NOT a benefit of String immutability?
choices: Identical literals can be pooled into one object
Strings use less memory than mutable character sequences
A method cannot alter a string you pass it
Strings are safe as hash keys
explanation: Immutability costs memory when you modify, since every change allocates. What it buys is safe sharing (hence the literal pool), safe passing with no defensive copy, safe hashing with a cacheable hash code, and thread safety with no coordination.
